cf.title: Fix slot synchronization with two_phase decoding enabled

input.subject: Fix slot synchronization with two_phase decoding enabled

verdict_reasoning: The HEAD fix is committed and the bug on 17 is real, so the goal is not in question. The decisive objection is prior-attempts-1: v19 makes a minor release reject `create subscription` statements that dumps from older 17.x contain. Messages #94 and #99 leave this open, and message #100 proposes a different design. The list must choose a design for 17 before code review of v19 is useful.

brief.title: Fix slot sync of two_phase logical slots on Postgres 17
brief.problem: After failover, a transaction prepared before two-phase decoding was enabled on a slot is not sent when it is committed on the promoted standby. The subscriber then fails with "prepared transaction with identifier ... does not exist". The cause is that the slot's two_phase_at is not synced to the standby, which affects users of logical replication who set both failover and two_phase.
brief.proposed_design: On HEAD the fix syncs two_phase_at and shows it in pg_replication_slots, but that catalog change cannot be backpatched to 17. For 17, the v19 patch rejects failover and two_phase together at slot and subscription creation, except in binary upgrade mode. It lets ALTER SUBSCRIPTION enable failover later, once two-phase state is enabled and the slot's restart_lsn has passed two_phase_at, and pg_dump writes such subscriptions with failover = false.
user_visible_surface: New pg_replication_slots column two_phase_at (pg_lsn), committed on HEAD only.
CREATE SUBSCRIPTION fails when both failover and two_phase are true.
pg_create_logical_replication_slot() and CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT fail when both failover and two_phase are set.
ALTER SUBSCRIPTION ... SET (failover = true) and ALTER_REPLICATION_SLOT fail while two-phase is pending or restart_lsn is before two_phase_at.
pg_dump emits failover = false for subscriptions that have both options enabled.
author_claims: The bug exists in 17 too, though it needs rarer steps to trigger there than on 18.
A catalog change is not acceptable in a minor release because this is not a security issue.
pg_upgrade can safely create slots with both options because it checks that slot changes are consumed and no prepared transactions exist.
Restoring an old 17.x dump into a fixed 17.x does not matter, since the docs recommend binary replacement for minor upgrades.
brief.thread_state: Amit Kapila committed the HEAD fix and a related assertion fix, and v19 for 17 has review from Shveta Malik, Ajin Cherian and Peter Smith. Sawada objects that dumps from older 17.x releases would fail to restore after the fix, and the last message proposes instead reporting failover as false until restart_lsn passes two_phase_at.
unclear: The thread does not say which approach the CF entry now tracks: v19 or the last message's idea of hiding failover in the view.
The proposal does not say what happens to existing 17 subscriptions that already have both options after a minor upgrade, beyond a release note.
Users of slots made with the SQL API can enable failover only with ALTER_REPLICATION_SLOT, and the thread accepts this without a simpler path.
No message after June 2025 shows whether anyone still plans to commit a fix for 17.

prior_attempts.title: Revert addition of PGDLLEXPORT in PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1 macro.
prior_attempts.quote: Third-party authors would not thank us for breaking their code in a minor release.
prior_attempts.reason:
This turns out not to be as harmless as I thought: MSVC will complain
if it sees an "extern" declaration without PGDLLEXPORT and then one with.
(Seems fairly silly, given that this can be changed after the fact by the
linker, but there you have it.)  Therefore, contrib modules that have
extern's for V1 functions in header files are falling over in the
buildfarm, since none of those externs are marked PGDLLEXPORT.

We might or might not conclude that we're willing to plaster those
declarations with PGDLLEXPORT in HEAD, but in any case there's no way we're
going to ship this change in the back branches.  Third-party authors would
not thank us for breaking their code in a minor release.  Hence, revert
the addition of PGDLLEXPORT (but let's keep the extra info in the comment).
If we do the other changes we can revert this commit in HEAD.

Per buildfarm.
prior_attempts.what_is_different: P23 reverted a macro change that broke extension builds in back branches. This proposal breaks restore of older 17.x dumps through new option checks, so P23 is only a loose analogy.

objections.title: Minor release makes dumps from older 17.x releases fail to restore
objections.failure_scenario: A user on 17.5 runs pg_dump for backup and the dump contains create subscription ... with (two_phase = true, failover = true). After a routine upgrade to the fixed 17.x, the restore stops with an error at that statement. The user finds this only when they need the backup.
objections.argument: [P23] records a revert because a change would break third-party code in a minor release. The same reason applies to a minor release that rejects SQL that older 17.x dumps contain. Amit raised the case in message #81 and Sawada in messages #83, #94 and #99. Messages #89 and #96 answer with the docs on binary replacement and on using the newer pg_dump. Message #99 notes that pg_dump is also used for plain backups, and message #100 proposes a different design, so the thread has not settled the point.
objections.author_must_show: How does a dump taken by 17.5 pg_dump restore on the fixed 17.x, or why is breaking that restore acceptable in a minor release?

precedents.title: Revert addition of PGDLLEXPORT in PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1 macro.

critic.reasoning: Messages #94 and #99 leave this open: binary replacement covers the upgrade path but not pg_dump backups taken on older 17.x. [P23] concerns extension build breakage, so it is at most a loose analogy and should not carry the argument.

other_surviving.title: pg_dump silently drops failover for subscriptions with both options
other_surviving.failure_scenario: An operator dumps and restores a database whose subscription has failover and two_phase on. The restored subscription has failover = false, and pg_dump gives no warning. Months later the publisher fails over, the slot was never synced to the standby, and the subscriber cannot continue.
other_surviving.argument: Message #81 proposes dumping failover = false and points to how pg_dump already handles connect = false. With connect = false, the user must take a visible step before anything runs. A failover property that is silently off looks like a working setup until the failover it was meant to protect against. The proposal says the restriction is documented, but pg_dump emits no warning and the dump contains no comment.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How does a user who restores such a dump learn that failover was turned off before the next publisher failover?

critic.reasoning: Message #81 weighed this and v18-0002 documents it, but the dump itself carries no notice. A restored subscription with failover off looks complete, unlike connect = false, which forces a visible step.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Existing 17.x slots with failover and two_phase stay exposed after the update
other_surviving.failure_scenario: A site created a subscription on 17.4 with failover = true and two_phase = true, then installs the fixed 17.x. The slot on the primary and its synced copy on the standby keep both flags, and two_phase_at is still not synced. After the next promotion, the subscriber fails with "prepared transaction ... does not exist".
other_surviving.argument: v19 only blocks new creation and new ALTER, so slot state already on disk passes through unchanged. Message #5 relies on a release note asking users to disable failover or recreate subscriptions. In 17 the user cannot see two_phase_at, so the restart_lsn > two_phase_at test from message #18 cannot be run to tell safe slots from unsafe ones.
other_surviving.author_must_show: How does a 17.x user find out, after a minor update, which existing failover slots with two_phase are still unsafe, given that two_phase_at is not visible?

critic.reasoning: Message #5 offers only release-note advice for existing slots, and v19 adds no check or warning for them. On 17 the view has no two_phase_at column, so a user cannot tell a safe slot from an unsafe one.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

other_surviving.title: Reporting failover as false in the view can drop already synced slots
other_surviving.failure_scenario: Under the idea in message #100, the primary starts reporting failover = false for a slot while restart_lsn is before two_phase_at. The standby's slotsync worker sees the remote slot as no longer failover and drops its local synced copy. A promotion in that window leaves the subscriber without a slot.
other_surviving.argument: Message #100 covers only newly created slots and calls the window short. The slotsync worker removes local synced slots that no longer match a failover remote slot, so already synced slots would also be dropped. The window lasts until the prepared transaction commits, and message #36 notes this can take a long time. Messages #4 and #5 also note the subscription's failover flag would still say true.
other_surviving.author_must_show: Under the view-hiding idea, what happens to a slot the standby has already synced when the primary starts reporting failover as false, and how is that kept safe?

critic.reasoning: Messages #13 and #14 show a slot can be synced before two_phase turns on after table sync, so message #100's claim that only new slots are affected does not hold. It applies only if the entry moves to the message #100 design.

other_surviving.not_ranked_reason: level 2 is above the failing level 1b: not evaluated (base-up stop rule)

refuted.title: Minor release turns valid CREATE SUBSCRIPTION and slot calls into errors
refuted.failure_scenario: A site keeps nightly pg_dump backups from 17.5 that contain subscriptions with failover = true and two_phase = true. After updating to a fixed 17.x, they restore one of these backups, and the CREATE SUBSCRIPTION statements fail. Provisioning scripts that call pg_create_logical_replication_slot() with both options also fail after the binary swap.
refuted.argument: v19 adds new errors to commands that 17.0 to 17.5 accept, and Sawada says in message #99 that he knows of no earlier minor-release break of this kind. Messages #89 and #96 answer that the docs recommend binary replacement for minor updates. That answer covers the upgrade method, but pg_dump is also used for backups, and the docs say a dump loads into the same or a newer server. [P23] records the rule against breaking users' code in a minor release.
refuted.author_must_show: Which earlier minor release made previously accepted DDL or dump output fail to load, and why is this case as justified?

precedents.title: Revert addition of PGDLLEXPORT in PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1 macro.

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1. The severity would also be fixable, since message #100 already proposes a design that avoids the new errors.

refuted.title: Existing subscriptions keep a state the fixed release forbids
refuted.failure_scenario: A site on 17.5 has a subscription with failover and two_phase on. It updates the binaries to the fixed 17.x and reads no release note. Its subscription still has both options and stays exposed to the lost-prepared-transaction bug, while new subscriptions with the same options are rejected.
refuted.argument: Message #5 relies on release-note advice to fix existing objects, and v19 contains no check or warning for them. The fixed server then holds catalog states that it does not let users create. Binary upgrade mode also keeps creating such slots on purpose (message #78). The resulting contract has three cases: forbidden for new objects, allowed in pg_upgrade, and left untouched for existing objects. The user-facing documentation does not explain this.
refuted.author_must_show: After the minor update, what tells an operator that an existing subscription with both options is still unsafe, other than the release notes?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of replication-ondisk-1, which states the same gap and adds that two_phase_at is not visible on 17.

refuted.title: Older 17.x dumps of subscriptions fail to restore on fixed 17.x
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator keeps nightly pg_dump backups from 17.5 that contain a subscription with failover = true and two_phase = true. They restore one into a 17.7 server and CREATE SUBSCRIPTION fails. The restore stops or skips the subscription, and they find out during a recovery.
refuted.argument: Message #81 raised this, and messages #94 and #99 say it is a compatibility break with no known precedent in a minor release. Messages #89 and #96 reply that the docs recommend binary replacement for minor updates. That answers how to update, but backups made with pg_dump also have to restore. v19-0002 fixes only dumps taken by the new pg_dump.
refuted.author_must_show: How will a dump taken by any released 17.x pg_dump, containing such a subscription, restore on the fixed release without manual editing?

precedents.title: Revert addition of PGDLLEXPORT in PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1 macro.

refuted.title: A rule set that exists only in 17 for the rest of its support life
refuted.failure_scenario: A later slotsync or slot-creation bug is fixed on HEAD and back-patched. The 17 branch also has v19's own checks: the binary-upgrade exception in slot creation, the restart_lsn versus two_phase_at check in ALTER_REPLICATION_SLOT, and the pg_dump rewrite. The back-patcher has to fit the fix around code HEAD does not have, and no test fails if one of these checks is bypassed.
refuted.argument: HEAD fixed the bug by syncing two_phase_at, so v19's checks never reach HEAD. In message #31 Amit asked to keep this code as close as possible between HEAD and the back branches, but v19 moves the two further apart than the first version did. Its safety also depends on pg_upgrade checking for unconsumed slot changes and prepared transactions (messages #78, #97), and nothing in slot.c enforces that dependency. Message #100 shows the 17 design is still open, so the extra code also lacks agreement.
refuted.author_must_show: Which 17-only checks would a future back-patched slotsync fix have to respect, and what test fails if the pg_upgrade guarantees they rely on change?

critic.reasoning: The scenario is a hypothetical future back-patch conflict, and messages #35, #55, #76 and #78 show tests for each new check, including the pg_upgrade case. Branch divergence follows from the no-catalog-change rule, which messages #5 and #87 weighed.

refuted.title: A minor release rejects dumps and configurations that 17.x accepted
refuted.failure_scenario: A user took a logical backup with pg_dump on an earlier 17.x, which emits failover = true and two_phase = true together. They restore it into a fixed 17.x, and CREATE SUBSCRIPTION fails during restore. They find out when they need the backup.
refuted.argument: Sawada said twice that this kind of break has no clear precedent in a minor release (messages #83, #99). The answer in messages #89 and #96 is that the docs recommend binary replacement for minor upgrades, but pg_dump is also used for backups, and that use is not addressed. The project has reverted a back-branch change because breaking existing users in a minor release was not acceptable [P23]. Existing subscriptions with both options are covered only by a release note (message #5), and message #100 proposes a different design to avoid this break.
refuted.author_must_show: How does a dump taken on an older 17.x with both options set restore into a fixed 17.x without manual editing?

precedents.title: Revert addition of PGDLLEXPORT in PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1 macro.

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of prior-attempts-1. Its point about existing subscriptions is covered by replication-ondisk-1.

refuted.title: Minor-release restriction for a bug no 17 user has reported
refuted.failure_scenario: An operator on 17.x has subscriptions with failover = true and two_phase = true and has never hit the bug. After a minor update, a new subscription with the same options fails, and a dump from an older 17.x does not restore. Their failover setup changes even though they were never exposed to the rare timing.
refuted.argument: On 17 the bug was found by testing, and its triggers are narrow: a pre-made slot with an advanced confirmed_flush, a prepare during initial table sync, or a race that needed a debugger (messages #4, #11, #17). The material has no -bugs report or field report from a 17 user. Messages #15 and #85 note that every user of the option combination pays, and messages #94 and #99 leave the dump breakage open. Message #91 accepts the restriction as "not ideal", but that does not show the trade is worth it for this branch.
refuted.author_must_show: Has any 17 user hit this in production, and why is a documented warning plus the recovery steps from message #17 not enough until such a report appears?

precedents.title: Revert addition of PGDLLEXPORT in PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1 macro.

critic.reasoning: Message #5 weighs the restriction against replication breaking after promotion, and message #11 shows a prepare during the default copy_data = true table sync triggers it. Message #30 narrowed the restriction; the dump part is a duplicate of prior-attempts-1.

touch_points.label: on-disk format / pg_upgrade
touch_points.reason: Binary upgrade mode keeps creating slots with both options, and existing slot state on disk passes through the minor update unchanged.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The fix changes slot sync to the standby and which logical slots may have failover enabled.

touch_points.label: catalog changes
touch_points.reason: The HEAD fix adds the two_phase_at column to pg_replication_slots, which is why it cannot go to 17.

touch_points.label: SQL-standard conflict or non-standard syntax
touch_points.reason: CREATE SUBSCRIPTION and pg_create_logical_replication_slot() start to reject an option combination that 17.0 to 17.5 accept.

touch_points.label: pg_dump / restore round-trip
touch_points.reason: pg_dump writes failover = false for subscriptions with both options, and older 17.x dumps fail to restore.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The entry targets 17 only and changes the behaviour of existing commands in a minor release.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The v19 checks exist only on the 17 branch, because HEAD fixes the bug by syncing two_phase_at.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: How does a dump taken by 17.5 pg_dump with failover = true and two_phase = true restore on the fixed 17.x without manual editing?
Which design does the CommitFest entry now track for 17: the v19 restriction, or the idea in message #100 of reporting failover as false?
After the minor update, how does a 17 user find which existing failover slots with two_phase are still unsafe, given that 17 does not show two_phase_at?
Under the message #100 idea, what happens to a slot the standby has already synced when the primary starts to report failover as false?
How does a user who restores a dump from the new pg_dump learn that failover was turned off for the subscription?

committability.owner_note: Amit Kapila committed the HEAD fix and reviews the 17 patch. The 17 change needs a committer who knows slot sync and who accepts the minor-release behaviour change.
committability.liability: The owner signs for a behaviour change in a minor release and for checks that exist only on the 17 branch until 17 reaches end of life. This includes any reports of dumps that no longer restore.
committability.author_follow_up: The author posted versions up to v19 and moved the entry to the next CommitFest in August 2025. The brief records no message after June 2025.

priority.reason: Only 17 users who set both failover and two_phase are affected, and the trigger on 17 is rare. v19 has review, but the dump restore objection is open and message #100 proposes another design, so the 17 design must be agreed first.

provisional_note: The v19 patches for 17 were not read, so the exact checks, the binary-upgrade exception and the pg_dump change are judged from the thread only. The message #100 idea has no patch to judge.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Logical decoding of two-phase transactions
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Alvaro Herrera, Arseny Sher, Petr Jelinek
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets logical decoding decode a two-phase transaction at PREPARE TRANSACTION time, with output plugin callbacks for prepare, commit prepared and abort prepared. To handle a concurrent ROLLBACK PREPARED during decoding, it first used decode groups that blocked the abort, then later versions stopped decoding when catalog access saw the transaction aborted.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was closed as Returned with feedback because no new patch version was posted after the January 2019 reviews. Those reviews reported open problems, among them that calling SnapBuildCommitTxn at PREPARE makes the catalog changes visible too early. Earlier, in July 2018, Robert Haas questioned whether blocking transaction aborts could work at all, and Andres Freund objected to a planned commit in April 2018.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I don't understand why this patch record has been kept aliv for so long,
since no new version has been sent in ages.  If this patch is really
waiting on the author, let's see the author do something.

precedents_retrieved.title: pgbench - break out initialization timing info by init phase
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgbench -i print a summary line with the elapsed time of each initialization phase (drop, create tables, insert, commit, primary keys, foreign keys, vacuum). The timing is measured inside each phase function and reported in a fixed order after all phases finish.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fabien COELHO supported the feature but asked for the durations in execution order, timing taken in the initialization loop, and separate begin and commit steps. The author agreed to some changes but posted no new version, so near the end of the v11 cycle the entry, waiting on author, was returned with feedback.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Since this submission is in Waiting on Author state I have marked it
Returned with Feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: hostorder and failover_timeout for libpq
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds two libpq connection parameters. `hostorder` (sequential or random) sets the order in which the hosts in a multi-host connection string are tried, and `failover_timeout` makes libpq loop over the hosts until one connects or the timeout expires.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The patch stopped applying, and the author did not rebase it or split it into separate `hostorder` and `failover_timeout` patches as Michael Paquier asked. Michael Paquier also doubted that a random mode alone justifies reworking libpq, and suggested that applications build their own connection strings. Tom Lane objected that the patch uses terms different from pgJDBC for nearly the same feature and overlaps two other patch threads, and these points were not addressed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As this hasn't been done, and Tom's questions haven't been addressed,
I'm marking this as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronize logical replication slots from primary to standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: A background worker on a physical standby periodically fetches logical replication slot information from the primary, so that after failover a logical subscriber finds up-to-date slots on the new primary. Later versions added synchronize_slot_names on the standby to pick which slots to sync, and standby_slot_names on the primary to hold logical replication back until the listed physical standbys catch up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch breaks the catalog_xmin guarantee: row versions still needed for logical decoding on the standby can be removed. He said it needs a mechanism such as the "Minimal logical decoding on standbys" patch, which the author said was not near ready. Reviewers also objected to the blocking wait and the per-commit work added to reorderbuffer.c, and to the worker-per-database design tied to the logical replication launcher. The author listed these and an open configuration design as significant jobs still to do.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch as-is just breaks one of the fundamental guarantees necessary for logical decoding, that no rows versions can be removed that are still required for logical decoding (signalled via catalog_xmin).

precedents_retrieved.title: pgbench - - break out timing data for initialization phases
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes pgbench record how long each initialization phase takes. At the end of initialization it prints the total time plus the times for insert, commit, vacuum and index creation.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Fabien COELHO said the patch might not work after another patch, ready for committer, that makes pgbench initialization customizable, and he asked the author to rebuild it on top of that patch. The author did not respond, and the patch needed a rebase, so Michael Paquier marked it returned with feedback for lack of activity.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
The patch needs as well a rebase, I am marking it as returned with
feedback per lack of activity.

precedents_retrieved.title: Patch to warn about any potential orphaned prepared transactions
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes autovacuum workers and manual VACUUM emit warnings for prepared transactions older than a set age, so administrators notice orphaned ones. It adds two settings: max_age_prepared_xacts for the age limit and prepared_xacts_vacuum_warn_timeout for how often autovacuum checks and warns.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas and Tom Lane did not want this functionality in the server, because a monitoring tool that queries pg_prepared_xacts already solves the problem and can be tailored to each site. Tom Lane also objected to putting the check in VACUUM: several autovacuum workers would warn about the same problem at once, and manual VACUUM output is rarely seen, so a log-scraping tool would still be needed. The author then withdrew the entry.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
To put that another way, any problem you can solve with this feature,
you can also solve without this feature.

precedents_retrieved.title: Prepare Transaction support for ON COMMIT DROP temporary tables
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch allows PREPARE TRANSACTION when every temporary table the transaction accessed was created with ON COMMIT DROP. PreCommit_on_commit_actions() drops those tables before the prepare, so the existing check against temporary tables in prepared transactions is relaxed for this case.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier showed that after creating an ON COMMIT DROP temp table and preparing, a client can disconnect but the backend stays waiting for a lock on its temporary schema until COMMIT PREPARED. The patch also does not handle the case where the temp table creates the session's temporary schema, and Tom Lane noted that tables without an ON COMMIT clause are not tracked. The entry was returned with feedback because more work was needed.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
This causes the client to think that the session is finished, but if
you look closer at the backend it is still pending to close until the
transaction is COMMIT PREPARED:

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronizing slots from primary to standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch runs the logical replication launcher on a standby and adds a per-database slotsync worker that periodically fetches slot state from the primary. The worker fast-forwards matching logical slots on the standby, and a new replication command lists the slots on the primary.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The thread does not record a design objection. The patch depended on the "logical decoding on standby" patch, which was not in the Commitfest, and Thomas Munro reported that the patches no longer applied on top of it. He asked for a rebased patch set, and the shown messages contain no reply from the author before the entry was returned.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: You patches no longer apply on top though.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Revert changes to CONCURRENTLY that "sped up" Xmin advance
Reverted commit(s): VACUUM: ignore indexing operations with CONCURRENTLY
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This reverts commit d9d076222f5b "VACUUM: ignore indexing operations
with CONCURRENTLY".

These changes caused indexes created with the CONCURRENTLY option to
miss heap tuples that were HOT-updated and HOT-pruned during the index
creation.  Before these changes, HOT pruning would have been prevented
by the Xmin of the transaction creating the index, but because this
change was precisely to allow the Xmin to move forward ignoring that
backend, now other backends scanning the table can prune them.  This is
not a problem for VACUUM (which requires a lock that conflicts with a
CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY operation), but HOT-prune can definitely
occur.  In other words, Xmin advancement was sped up, but at the cost of
corrupting the resulting index.

Regrettably, this means that the new feature in PG14 that RIC/CIC on
very large tables no longer force VACUUM to retain very old tuples goes
away.  We might try to implement it again in a later release, but for
now the risk of indexes missing tuples is too high and there's no easy
fix.

Backpatch to 14, where this change appeared.

precedents_retrieved.title: Revert addition of PGDLLEXPORT in PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1 macro.
precedents_retrieved.summary: Revert addition of PGDLLEXPORT in PG_FUNCTION_INFO_V1 macro.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
This turns out not to be as harmless as I thought: MSVC will complain
if it sees an "extern" declaration without PGDLLEXPORT and then one with.
(Seems fairly silly, given that this can be changed after the fact by the
linker, but there you have it.)  Therefore, contrib modules that have
extern's for V1 functions in header files are falling over in the
buildfarm, since none of those externs are marked PGDLLEXPORT.

We might or might not conclude that we're willing to plaster those
declarations with PGDLLEXPORT in HEAD, but in any case there's no way we're
going to ship this change in the back branches.  Third-party authors would
not thank us for breaking their code in a minor release.  Hence, revert
the addition of PGDLLEXPORT (but let's keep the extra info in the comment).
If we do the other changes we can revert this commit in HEAD.

Per buildfarm.

roaster_notes.note: No precedent row proposes the same fix. Inside the thread, message #4 first raised the idea of showing failover as false, message #5 dropped it as hard to explain, and message #100 brings it back. Message #5 also cites an earlier catalog backpatch that was done only for a CVE.
Objections were raised. The SQL-API-only ALTER_REPLICATION_SLOT path was not raised because the thread accepted it as a restriction in message #47.

The proposal has no privilege or exposure aspect. The new two_phase_at column shows an LSN of the same kind as restart_lsn and confirmed_flush_lsn, which pg_replication_slots already shows. The v19 changes only add restrictions, and the binary-upgrade exception applies only inside pg_upgrade, so no role gains a new capability.
Hot-path cost is not a concern here: the checks run only at slot or subscription creation and when the slot or subscription is altered.

This is a bug fix for slot sync on Postgres 17, and no existing feature, extension or external tool closes the gap. The only existing workaround is to set failover = false by hand, and that is exactly what the patch enforces, so nothing from this angle applies.
The HEAD fix answers a real, reproduced bug and is out of scope here. The demand concern applies only to the 17 backpatch.
